title: Prepared-solve lifecycle audit of the original HLINK02 failure
source_findings: Modflow6PreparedSolveSession.timestep_ready_for_finalize() is true only after finalize_prepared_solve(): finalized must be true and solve_open must be false.
The original HLINK02 harness called timestep_ready_for_finalize() before finalize_prepared_solve(). That readiness check was therefore structurally false independent of the MODFLOW convergence flag.
The original HLINK02 loop did not persist a separate converged boolean before the impossible readiness assertion, so run 35578161179 cannot be used to conclude that MODFLOW itself failed to converge.
HLINK02D inherited the same ordering error by storing ready=timestep_ready_for_finalize() before finalize_prepared_solve() and later requiring that stale false value.
HLINK01 uses the correct sequence: require convergence, finalize_prepared_solve(), then check timestep_ready_for_finalize(), then finalize_time_step_once().
The shared one-cell build_model helper is bit-for-bit identical between the qualified HLINK01 execution commit and the current branch.
The HLINK02 test file is bit-for-bit identical between failure run 35578161179 and the pre-repair current branch, so the audit addresses the exact failing harness.
MODFLOW 6.8.0 STO sto_fc reads this%sy(n) directly when assembling SyTerms; no separate same-value-write cache/dirty-state mechanism was identified in the audited source path.

hlink02: require that convergence flag before solve finalization
keep all storage formulas, RCLOSE, head tolerance, mass tolerance and outer iteration rules unchanged
hlink02d: for converged variants call finalize_prepared_solve() before evaluating the preregistered readiness output

forbidden_inference: Do not mark HLINK02 scientifically qualified from source review alone.
Do not infer the write_sy/rclose outcome before live execution.
Do not change production MODFLOW6 or F-GC code from this research harness repair.
